readmeExcerpt:
Open Mercato Readiness Scanner

Find production-readiness gaps before you deploy.

Read-only readiness scans for applications built with create-mercato-app.
Check local configuration, get actionable findings, and export reports for your release process.

```bash npx mercato-readiness-scanner scan . ```

Quick start · Reports · CI · Rules · Framework docs · Discord

```mermaid flowchart LR A["📁 Your Open Mercato app"] --> B["🔎 Static readiness scan"] B --> C["🛡️ Configuration & security"] B --> D["🚀 Deployment & operations"] C --> E["📋 Findings & remediation"] D --> E E --> F["💻 Terminal"] E --> G["📝 Markdown"] E --> H["🔧 JSON / CI"] style B fill:#b4f372,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1b1b1b style E fill:#bc9aff,color:#1b1b1b,stroke:#1b1b1b ``` `scan` is read-only. The explicit [`apply`](#apply-the-remediations) command can add safe fixes to a git working tree. ## Quick start You need **Node.js 24 or newer** and an application created with [`create-mercato-app`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/create-mercato-app). Run from your application directory: ```bash cd my-open-mercato-app npx mercato-readiness-scanner scan . ``` Or pass the application path from another directory: ```bash npx mercato-readiness-scanner scan /path/to/open-mercato-app ``` No global install is required. To see all options: ```bash npx mercato-readiness-scanner --help ``` The default terminal report groups failed, review-only, skipped, and passing checks with `❌`, `⚠️`, `⏭️`, and `✅` markers. Every actionable result includes remediation text and a permanent rule-documentation URL. ## Check credentials and encryption keys Credential inspection runs automatically in every scan: ```bash npx mercato-readiness-scanner@0.2.1 scan . --fail-on high ``` `scan` inspects root `.env`, `.env.production`, `.env.local`, and `.env.production.local` files, visible runtime settings, and supported Compose service environments. It checks every detected credential-like setting, including JWT/signing secrets, database and Redis passwords, other service passwords, API tokens/keys, and tenant encryption fallback/master keys. Database URL passwords, copied template credentials, and `${NAME:-default}` fallbacks are included. File contents remain in memory; findings contain variable names and fixed reasons, never credential values. Application code and shell expressions are never executed. `apply` does not read or change these values. | Finding | Behavior | |---|---| | ❌ Default, placeholder, or copied template credential | Critical failure | | ❌ Short, repeated, or predictable credential | Critical failure | | ❌ Weak tenant encryption fallback/master key | Critical failure | | ❌ Development fallback enabled without an explicit tenant key | Critical failure | | ⚠️ No complete KMS configuration | Configure Vault;
